summary: Browser redirect loader distributed via npm/jsDelivr; no installer-side execution
details: px8my ships a single browser-only module (px.js) that injects a fullscreen iframe pointing at https://mfmz.fielop05.cn/H.html?c=0gjr. package.json declares no preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare hooks and main is DOM code that would throw under Node (document.write / document.body), so `npm install` and `require()` of this package do not execute the redirect against a Node installer. A shipped maintenance script (update_px8my.sh) rotates the destination domain, bumps the version, republishes to npm, and purges the jsDelivr cache, indicating the package's purpose is redistributing a mutable browser redirect through the npm to jsDelivr CDN chain to end-users who load npm/px8my/px.js in a browser. The maintenance script is not wired into any lifecycle hook and does not run on install. Under this engine's installer-centric threat model, there is no exfiltration, RCE, credential theft, silent-relay of installer data, install-time destruction, or attacker benefit against the party running `npm install`; the abuse target is browser end-users of the CDN, not the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
